subject: kimi-cli
title: D-Mail: the model folds its own context by reverting to a named checkpoint with a model-authored payload, at zero LLM cost
evidence: src/kimi_cli/tools/dmail/dmail.md; src/kimi_cli/soul/denwarenji.py; src/kimi_cli/soul/kimisoul.py:1315-1335 (BackToTheFuture), :1100-1105 (revert+recheckpoint); src/kimi_cli/soul/context.py:137-190 (revert_to with journal rotation)
one_why: Second compaction tier that needs no summarizer call: agent rewrites its own history at a step where it notices waste (huge file read, dead-end debugging), and the tool text is explicitly honest that filesystem state is NOT reverted -- unlike pi's branch summaries this is agent-initiated, not system-initiated.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Graduated repeat-call ladder (reminders at 3/5/8, hard turn-stop at 12) plus same-step dedup that awaits the original task and copies its result
evidence: src/kimi_cli/soul/toolset.py:117-167 (ladder), :176-199 (canonical-JSON arg keys), :370-375 (same-step await-and-copy), :430-452; src/kimi_cli/soul/kimisoul.py:1330-1337 (force_stop_turn); tests/core/test_kimisoul_repeat.py
one_why: Most complete loop breaker found: streaks survive across steps via canonicalized args, escalation is prompt-side before the circuit trips, and parallel identical calls within one step are collapsed instead of double-executed -- crush's breaker is a single-shot abort by comparison.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Agent flows declared as D2/Mermaid fenced blocks in SKILL.md, parsed into task/decision graphs; the ralph loop is just a synthesized 2-node flow
evidence: src/kimi_cli/skill/__init__.py:645-660; src/kimi_cli/skill/flow/d2.py, mermaid.py; src/kimi_cli/soul/kimisoul.py:1787-1845 (FlowRunner.ralph_loop), :1862-1963 (edge-choice execution + re-prompt); klips/klip-10-agent-flow.md
one_why: Deterministic multi-turn control flow that end users can author as pictures; decision nodes re-prompt on invalid <choice> instead of crashing, and the notorious ralph-loop is expressed as data (BEGIN->R1->R2 self-loop->END) rather than a separate runner.

subject: kimi-cli
title: ChaosChatProvider: a fault-injection decorator wrapping any real provider, deterministic-configured, used to test retry/recovery paths in the live loop
one_why: Beyond scripted responses: transient-connection/auth failures are injected into a real Kimi provider and the test asserts the loop's 401-refresh-once / connection-recovery-once ladder (kimisoul.py:1657-1730) actually unwinds correctly.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Approvals are action-name session-cached and ContextVar-sourced: approving an action retroactively resolves same-action pending requests, and turn end cancels orphaned approvals
one_why: Approval identity travels with the execution context (foreground turn vs subagent), so backgrounded work can surface approvals on the root wire hub without leaking them past the turn that created them; feedback-aware rejections get anti-bypass instruction text for subagents (approval.py:76-100).

subject: kimi-cli
title: All fs+exec tools go through a kaos backend interface with local, SSH, and ACP-host implementations -- in ACP mode the agent's shell and file tools run on the IDE host's terminal APIs
evidence: packages/kaos/src/kaos/local.py, ssh.py:61,276; src/kimi_cli/acp/kaos.py:44-165 (ACPProcess over terminal_create/wait/output), :165-259; src/kimi_cli/acp/session.py:159 (set_current_kaos); klips/klip-2-acpkaos.md
one_why: The whole tool surface is host-agnostic by construction: the same Shell/Read/Write tools transparently execute in an SSH box or inside the editor's own terminal/filesystem bridge, which no other reviewed subject does -- rival IDE integrations re-implement tools per surface.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Background tasks run as detached worker processes with heartbeats, control-file polling, stale reconciliation, and Windows process-tree kill
evidence: src/kimi_cli/background/worker.py:21-40; src/kimi_cli/background/manager.py:422-483 (stale_after, reconcile); background/store.py; kimisoul.py:1131-1146 (notification injection with pre-delivery reconcile); tests/core/test_background_agent_kill.py
one_why: Crash-aware durability for bg bash+agent tasks: after a CLI restart, reconcile() marks orphaned workers stale before notifications are claimed, so the model never waits on a phantom task -- amazon-q's delegate tool has the spawn half but none of the reconciliation half.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Two cooperating JSONL journals: versioned wire.jsonl (protocol-versioned envelope header) for UI replay and context.jsonl with inline _checkpoint/_usage markers that turn-aware truncation slices for /undo and /fork
evidence: src/kimi_cli/wire/file.py:19-30; src/kimi_cli/soul/context.py:124-135,271-340 (marker records, tolerant replay); src/kimi_cli/session_fork.py:1-30; tests_e2e/test_wire_sessions.py; tests/core/test_session_fork.py
one_why: Token accounting is embedded in the journal itself (_usage records reset the pending-estimate on restore) so crash-resume reconstructs near-exact context usage, and malformed lines are skipped rather than failing the load -- the journal doubles as the compaction trigger's source of truth.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Four host contracts off one soul: single+multi-session ACP server, versioned wire JSON-RPC with host-provided external tools, stream-json headless, and an OpenAPI web backend -- and kimi term dogfoods its own ACP server
evidence: src/kimi_cli/acp/AGENTS.md:13-49; src/kimi_cli/wire/server.py:26-33 (HookRequest/ToolCallRequest); KLIP-12 (klips/klip-12-wire-initialize-external-tools.md); docs/en/reference/kimi-term.md:9-13; docs/en/reference/kimi-command.md:98-106; sdks/kimi-sdk + .github/workflows/release-kimi-sdk.yml
one_why: External hosts can inject their own tools mid-turn (KLIP-12) and receive hook callbacks over the wire -- nanocoder proved ACP dogfooding for one plugin; kimi-cli spread the same event stream across four contracts plus a published SDK.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Hooks exist with the full Claude-shaped event vocabulary but can only come from the global config file, so a cloned repo cannot plant hook commands
evidence: src/kimi_cli/config.py:276-278 (get_config_file = share dir only); src/kimi_cli/hooks/config.py:5-19; src/kimi_cli/hooks/runner.py:78-81 (permissionDecision deny); src/kimi_cli/hooks/engine.py:244-246 (PreToolUse block is fail-closed)
one_why: Not advertised as a security feature, but the config-scoping accident means repo-borne hook RCE -- the hole several rivals have -- is structurally absent; PreToolUse denial is honored before the approval prompt and telemetry failure cannot downgrade the block.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Canonicalized workspace containment on read/glob with an explicit /add-dir escape hatch persisted in session state, and a distinct approval action for edits outside the workspace
evidence: src/kimi_cli/tools/file/read.py:86-94; glob.py:87-101; tools/file/__init__.py:13 (edit-file-outside action); src/kimi_cli/soul/agent.py:243-261 (prune stale additional_dirs on restore); tests/test_additional_dirs_state.py
one_why: Containment is canonical-path based (no sibling-prefix escape), out-of-workspace edits are not silently allowed but mapped to their own approval action name -- so per-action session caching degrades to least-privilege by default.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Graceful sunset engineering: final releases convert the CLI's own entry points into a redirector that downloads and runs the successor's installer, plus a tested tombstone package
evidence: CHANGELOG.md 1.51.0/1.52.0 entries ('Running kimi with no arguments now directly downloads and runs the Kimi Code install script'); HEAD commit 9ab1286 'short-circuit entry points to a Kimi Code installer (#2666)'; packages/kimi-code/src/kimi_code/__init__.py; tests/core/test_kimi_code_tombstone.py; SECURITY.md:1
one_why: A field template for killing a live product: no-fix SECURITY banner, tombstone package that prints migration instructions and exits 1, and the binary itself funnels stragglers to the successor -- archived:true remote-verified, which is also why this review's band is capped at B by rule (b).
